summary: Authors interactive spreadsheets (tabular cells, formatting, formulas), optionally with assessed cells the learner fills in, from natural-language descriptions.
in_scope: Multiple sheets in one item, with tabs and a sheet menu to move between them
Column / row / region styling: width, alignment, fonts, colors, borders
Cell text, formatting, and per-cell properties
Formulas (SUM, AVERAGE, ROUND, POWER, MAX, MIN, ABS, IF, arithmetic)
Parameterized values that vary per render (templateVariablesRecords)
Assessed cells: value-equivalence, formula-equivalence, per-cell points and partial credit
Schema-validated output suitable for hosting as a Learnosity custom question via L0158
out_of_scope: Authoring assessment ITEMS or QUESTIONS as content — reading-comprehension or ELA items, multiple-choice / EBSR / short-answer questions, passages, stems, answer keys, or rubric-scored prose. L0179 authors a spreadsheet INTERACTION (cells and formulas the learner completes), NOT question items; assessment-item authoring belongs to a dedicated assessment dialect, not a spreadsheet
Any tabular tool that isn't a spreadsheet (database tables, CSV editors, query builders, pivot dashboards, Airtable-style relational tables, gantt charts)
Charts and visualizations (pie, bar, line) — charting belongs in a separate dialect

Pivot tables, cross-sheet FORMULA references, or aggregations across sheets. Several sheets in one item ARE supported; what is not is a formula on one sheet reading a cell on another (=Sheet2!A1), or a total computed across sheets
External data imports (CSV, database, HTTP ingestion)
Macros, user-defined functions, or event hooks — formula coverage is fixed
Activity-level assembly (sequencing multiple spreadsheets into a lesson)
Host-app embedding (React/Vite mount inside an LMS) — handled by the host runtime
